en.summary: France's news landscape combines national newspapers based in Paris, a large public broadcasting system and strong regional dailies. Le Monde, Le Figaro and Libération are the main national titles, and Agence France-Presse is one of the world's three global news agencies. Public broadcasters France Télévisions and Radio France run the franceinfo news service, while private channels such as BFMTV offer 24-hour news. Ownership of private media is concentrated among a few large industrial and financial groups, which is a recurring subject of public debate. Mediapart, a subscriber-funded site, is known for investigations into politics and finance. Regional dailies such as Ouest-France, the country's largest newspaper by circulation, cover their regions in depth. The state supports the press through direct and indirect subsidies.

faq.q: What are the main national news outlets in France?
faq.a: The main national outlets in the directory include Le Monde, Le Figaro, Libération, Agence France-Presse and franceinfo. The Top National News column lists them in editorial order.

faq.q: Which French news sites are free to read?
faq.a: Free-to-read outlets include Agence France-Presse, franceinfo, BFMTV, France Inter and RFI. The paywall model of every outlet is shown next to its name.

faq.q: Which French outlets are publicly or state funded?
faq.a: Public-service outlets include Agence France-Presse, franceinfo, France Inter and RFI. Ownership is labeled on every outlet in the directory.

faq.q: Where can I find regional news in France?
faq.a: Regional coverage in the directory comes from Le Parisien (Île-de-France), Ouest-France (Brittany and western France), Le Progrès (Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes), La Voix du Nord (Hauts-de-France) and Sud Ouest (Nouvelle-Aquitaine). The Regional & Local column lists every regional outlet.

general-news.intro: National news in France comes from Paris-based dailies, the AFP news agency and public broadcasting. Each outlet below shows its paywall model and owner.

economy.intro: French business news is covered by a leading business daily, business magazines and personal finance titles following companies, the CAC 40 and economic policy.

sports.intro: French sports media is led by a national sports daily and covers football, cycling and rugby through broadcasters, magazines and specialized sites.

investigative.intro: Investigative journalism in France includes a subscriber-funded news site, a nonprofit investigative outlet and fact-checking desks at the national news agency and a leading daily.

regional.intro: Regional dailies are a pillar of the French press, with dozens of local editions. The titles below cover the west, Lyon, the north, the southwest and Provence.

politics.intro: French political coverage follows the Élysée, the government and both chambers of Parliament through national dailies, public radio, a parliamentary channel and policy-focused subscription newsrooms.
